title: The Abbott and Costello Show
paragraphs: Comedy-variety archive centered on Bud Abbott and Lou Costello. The GRH snapshot mixes episodes of their regular 1942-49 prime-time series with earlier appearances/summer-series material and specials. Descriptive file titles are archive labels, not official historical episode titles.

GRH documents the program through Kate Smith appearances (February 3, 1938 to June 28, 1940) on [[org|org.8480b75bc0c36e4b|CBS Radio Network]], Time to Smile (July 3, 1940 to September 25, 1940) on [[org|org.f2f0561f0ce2ddc5|NBC Radio Network]], Chase and Sanborn appearances (April 6, 1941 to June 28, 1942) on [[org|org.f2f0561f0ce2ddc5|NBC Radio Network]], and NBC Camel years (October 8, 1942 to June 26, 1947) on [[org|org.f2f0561f0ce2ddc5|NBC Radio Network]].

Among the most extensively documented contributors in the GRH holdings are Bud Abbott (performer on 43 recordings), Lou Costello (performer on 43 recordings), Ken Niles (announcer on 33 recordings and performer on 1 recording), Connie Haines (performer on 33 recordings and vocalist on 3 recordings), Freddie Rich and His Orchestra (performer on 24 recordings), Elvia Allman (performer on 18 recordings), and Mel Blanc (performer on 14 recordings).

plain_text:
Comedy-variety archive centered on Bud Abbott and Lou Costello. The GRH snapshot mixes episodes of their regular 1942-49 prime-time series with earlier appearances/summer-series material and specials. Descriptive file titles are archive labels, not official historical episode titles.

GRH documents the program through Kate Smith appearances (February 3, 1938 to June 28, 1940) on CBS Radio Network, Time to Smile (July 3, 1940 to September 25, 1940) on NBC Radio Network, Chase and Sanborn appearances (April 6, 1941 to June 28, 1942) on NBC Radio Network, and NBC Camel years (October 8, 1942 to June 26, 1947) on NBC Radio Network.

Among the most extensively documented contributors in the GRH holdings are Bud Abbott (performer on 43 recordings), Lou Costello (performer on 43 recordings), Ken Niles (announcer on 33 recordings and performer on 1 recording), Connie Haines (performer on 33 recordings and vocalist on 3 recordings), Freddie Rich and His Orchestra (performer on 24 recordings), Elvia Allman (performer on 18 recordings), and Mel Blanc (performer on 14 recordings).

The program is also connected in the archive to NBC Radio Network (broadcast on network), KFI (aircheck from station), and Armed Forces Radio Service (rebroadcast by).

Its indexed subjects and listening characteristics include Hollywood, movies and celebrity guests, everyday jobs, money and domestic mishaps, music and variety performance, detective and crime parody, western parody and frontier comedy, and wartime service, military and home-front comedy.

GRH also places the series in documented historical contexts including Sponsor-driven network comedy, Wartime popular comedy and service culture, Hollywood guest-star variety culture, and Postwar shift to transcribed/cooperative network radio.

Programs with especially strong personnel connections in the GRH knowledge graph include Lux Radio Theatre (22 shared credited people), Duffy's Tavern (17 shared credited people), Screen Directors Playhouse (11 shared credited people), Sealtest Variety Theater (9 shared credited people), and The Phil Harris-Alice Faye Show (7 shared credited people).
